data.name: Jayita
data.gender_notes: Jayita is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Jayita is derived from the Sanskrit word 'jay' meaning victory or triumph. It is a name of great significance in Hindu mythology and culture, representing the triumph of good over evil and the victory of the human spirit. The name Jayita carries the meaning “Victory, Triumph” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jayita usually hope their child will grow to embody victory, triumph and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the inner victory and triumph of the soul over worldly desires and challenges.
data.etymology: Jayita belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Victory, Triumph.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jayita total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Jayita was a famous courtesan in ancient India. The name Jayita carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Jayita was a renowned courtesan who lived during the Gupta Empire in ancient India. She is mentioned in the works of the poet Kalidasa, particularly in his play 'Shakuntala'.
